documents.title: Board Meeting Intimation for Considering And Approving, Among Other Matters, The Unaudited Financial Results Of The Company For The Quarter Ended June 30, 2026.
Shareholder Meeting / Postal Ballot-Outcome of EGM

analysis.summary: SK Minerals & Additives Limited reported a 50% revenue growth to Rs. 318 crores for FY26, accompanied by higher EBITDA margins and manufacturing capacity expansion. Management discussed strategic raw material sourcing, capacity utilization of food and feed segments, and scaling up the new polymer additives and halogen-free flame retardant business. The company outlined plans for a Rs. 20 crores capex over the next two years to expand manufacturing capabilities toward 18,000 metric tons.

guidance.claim: Management expects to increase the manufacturing contribution to turnover to 50% in the next two to three years.
guidance.quote: Currently, 23% of our revenue comes from the manufacturing capabilities, but in the next two to three years, we want to scale the manufacturing contribution to turnover to 50%, with overall increase in turnover also.

guidance.claim: The company expects manufacturing margins from polymer additives to be approximately 40%.
guidance.quote: Currently, in terms of the manufacturing margins, we are standing at 30% approximately, whereas from polymer additives, we feel that the margins would be 40%.

demand_outlook.claim: Demand for the company's products was driven by a mix of volume growth and price increases.
demand_outlook.quote: So, it is a mix of increase in price and volume driven sales.

demand_outlook.claim: The company is experiencing demand from foreign buyers for its polymer additives.
demand_outlook.quote: This product is good and we have received interest from foreign buyers also.

capex_expansion.claim: The company acquired 9.6 acres of land for developing polymer additives and polymer compound facilities.
capex_expansion.quote: First of all, this 9.6 acre land which we have taken is for developing our polymer additives and polymer compound facility, whereas specified that in next 12 to 18 months, we will be taking our manufacturing capabilities to 18,000 metric tons.

capex_expansion.claim: The company aims to increase its total capacity to 18,000 metric tons in a phased manner over the next 12 to 18 months.
capex_expansion.quote: Basically, we are looking at total capacity of 18,000 metric tons including all the current capacity and this we are going to increase in the phased manner in the next 18 months.

margins_costs.claim: EBITDA margins increased from 9% to 10% and PAT increased from 5% to 6% in the last financial year.
margins_costs.quote: our EBITDA margins have increased from 9% to 10% and PAT has increased from 5% to 6%.

margins_costs.claim: Margin contraction in the second half was caused by an increase in raw material prices from January onwards.
margins_costs.quote: It is because of the increase in the prices of raw materials. And as I have said prices have increased specifically, from January onwards, the prices of raw material have increased.

margins_costs.claim: Gross margins from manufacturing stand at approximately 30%, whereas trading products yield 21%.
margins_costs.quote: So, in terms of gross margin, which we make from manufacturing, right now it's 30%. Whereas, in terms of our trading product, it is 21%.

orders_capacity.claim: Current total installed capacity stands at 6,600 metric tons.
orders_capacity.quote: The current capacity is 6600 metric tons.

orders_capacity.claim: Current capacity utilization is approximately 95% in the food and feed segment.
orders_capacity.quote: current capacity utilization is approximately 95% in food and feed segment and we have set up one food segment also which is almost optimally used.

capital_allocation.claim: The company has started invoice discounting facilities for buyers to help reduce the working capital cycle.
capital_allocation.quote: we are trying to discount the material which we are invoice discounting facility we have started to take for our buyers.

capital_allocation.claim: The company plans to fund its capex using bank credit lines and unutilized IPO proceeds.
capital_allocation.quote: We have the credit lines available for CAPEX from the banks also. And we have some part of the IPO proceeds which we have raised for CAPEX. So, we will utilize both for taking our capacity to next level to 18,000 metric tons.

risks_headwinds.claim: Geopolitical scenarios and transportation timelines impact the import of trading materials as stock dries up.
risks_headwinds.quote: In terms of the import trading, yes, it has impacted because we have three months’ stock always available with us. So, that stock is getting dried up.

management_commitments.claim: The company aims to scale its manufacturing capacity to 18,000 metric tons in a phased manner over the next 12 to 18 months.
management_commitments.quote: So, from the current capacity of 600 metric ton, we will take it to 18,000 metric ton in phase manner of next 12 to 18 months.

management_commitments.claim: The company plans to file three patents in the next six months.
management_commitments.quote: But in next six months, we will try to file three patents.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
